sources.name: Simple Features Access Part 1: Common Architecture 1.2.1
verified_facts: A Polygon is a planar surface with one exterior boundary and zero or more interior boundaries; each interior boundary defines a hole.
Valid polygon boundaries are LinearRings; boundary rings do not cross and may meet only tangentially at isolated points.
Within requires the first geometry to be wholly included without interior or boundary points entering the exterior of the second geometry.
semantic_limits: An Intersects result may include boundary-only contact and is not equivalent to parcel interior containment.
A syntactically decodable polygon must still pass topology validation before raster sampling.

sources.name: Filter Encoding 2.0 Encoding Standard with Corrigendum
verified_facts: Filter Encoding defines Equals, Disjoint, Touches, Within, Overlaps, Crosses, Intersects, Contains, DWithin, Beyond and BBOX spatial predicates.
A Within B implies B Contains A under the referenced Simple Features semantics.
BBOX is a compact NOT Disjoint test against an envelope and therefore selects every geometry that spatially interacts with the box.
semantic_limits: BBOX is a coarse candidate prefilter and does not prove exact point-in-polygon or polygon-within-polygon containment.
A service must advertise which spatial operators it supports; unsupported predicates must not be silently substituted.

sources.name: Common Query Language CQL2 1.0
verified_facts: A CQL2 filter evaluates each resource to true, false or null; only true results belong to the selected result set.
The basic spatial class requires S_INTERSECTS for points and bounding boxes, while the richer spatial class adds S_WITHIN, S_CONTAINS and other DE-9IM predicates.
CQL2 supports text and JSON encodings and can carry an explicit filter CRS for non-default coordinate literals.
semantic_limits: S_INTERSECTS must not be substituted for S_WITHIN when exact containment is required.
A successful filter evaluates query semantics only; it does not validate HMLR topology, LiDAR provenance or numeric elevation accuracy.

sources.name: INSPIRE Data Specification on Elevation Technical Guidelines v3.3.0
verified_facts: A DTM describes the bare surface, while a DSM includes heights of objects such as vegetation and man-made structures.
Elevation values are referenced to a specified vertical reference or datum, and the grid representation is a coverage over rectified grid positions.
A void value means the source dataset contains no corresponding value or none can be derived at reasonable cost; a void reason should be supplied where possible.
semantic_limits: Void or missing elevation cells must be excluded from parcel min/max calculations and must never be interpreted as zero elevation.
INSPIRE interoperability guidance does not prove that a particular EA tile, HMLR polygon or candidate measurement is correct.
